For various ammonia technology suppliers, net energy consumption ranges from as high as 32.8 GJ/tonne NH (for the Humphreys and Glasgow Process when CO is 3 2 recovered) to as low as 26.8 GJ/tonne NH (for the Jacobs Plus Ammonia Technology 3 when steam is exported) (Kermeli, et al., 2017). Overall, the net energy consumptions of the study cases are within that reported by ammonia technology suppliers. • The major contributors to the plant power requirement are ammonia production, air compressors, and the air separation unit. The largest compressor loads are driven by steam, including the ammonia plant compressors and refrigeration system as well as the air compressor for Case 1. 3 COMPARISON OF COMMERCIAL, STATE-OF-THE-ART, FOSSIL-BASED AMMONIA PRODUCTION • Most of the water consumption can be attributed to high pressure steam generation for Case 1 and the cooling tower for Case 2 and Case 3. Global warming potential (GWP) results The primary observations that can be made are as follows: • Case 1 results in the highest GWP, which is an expected result given there is no carbon capture equipment included in Case 1. • Despite the lower natural gas consumption in Case 3, Case 3 still results in a higher GWP than Case 2 due to a lower CO capture rate. This result is consistent with observations 2 in hydrogen production GWP results. • GWP results are slightly higher when using Midwest regional electricity and natural gas data than when using U.S. average values. • All ammonia production scenarios have significant high-end uncertainty, driven by conventional natural gas extracted from the Uinta basin. Levelized cost of ammonia The primary observations that can be made are as follows: • The largest contributor to the BEC for Case 1 and Case 2 is the ammonia production section. Adding capture to the SMR case results in a 29 percent increase in the BEC, with most of the increase due to the post-combustion CO capture system and CO 2 2 compression system. The largest contributor to the BEC for Case 3 is the air separation unit. • In Exhibit ES-6, the error bars depicted represent the uncertainty range for AACE Class 5 estimates, which are -25 to +50 percent of capital costs.
